<div class="wv-epigraph">{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|“And, if we tried anything, you know Indirial would kill us both.”}}<div class="wv-epigraph-cite">{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|— ''House of Blades'', chapter 11}}</div></div>
''See also: [[Indirial Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Indirial is the [[Overlord of Cana]] and a highly trusted, long-standing servant to the King. Though he holds significant [[Authority|authority]] that places him second only to the monarch, he maintains a respectful relationship with royalty through formal gestures like bowing. Physically, he appears to be in his late thirties or early forties despite being in his fifties, possessing tanned skin, dark eyes, and short dark hair. He is frequently seen wearing shirts with the sleeves removed to display black chain tattoos that wrap around his arms, and he carries a gold medallion featuring a dark amethyst. A formidable warrior and one of the [[Incarnations]], Indirial is characterized by a personality that balances a cheerful, easygoing demeanor with constant vigilance. He is known to be a lethal combatant who will carry out any execution ordered by his King without hesitation. Beyond his military and political roles, he is a father to a daughter who is training in swordsmanship. He possesses extensive knowledge of various individuals and locations, including connections to [[Myria]] and the [[Travelers]].}}

== Appearance ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Indirial is a dark-skinned individual with dark hair and violet eyes. He wears a black [[Nye cloak]] and has shadowy black chain marks crawling up his forearms. Additionally, his left hand is covered by a spiked [[black gauntlet]] known as a [[Valinhall gatecrawler]].}}

== Personality ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|A trusted servant and the oldest confidant to [[Leah's father]], Indirial is a cautious figure who acts as a voice of warning. He is a dedicated warrior and Overlord who commands the [[Tartarus]] group and serves under the [[Authority|authority]] of [[King Zakareth VI]]. While he has shown sympathy toward [[Leah]], he is also a formidable combatant willing to kill those who threaten him.}}

== Relationships ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Indirial is the son of Aleias and [[Kalman]], and he has a daughter named [[Elaina]]. He serves as the most trusted servant to [[Leah's father]] and is a subject of [[King Zakareth the Sixth]]. Indirial has connections to [[Leah]], whom he has provided information and sympathy to, as well as [[Simon]], whom he previously saved. He is also associated with [[Kathrin]] and the old master, has spoken with Feiora, and discussed strategy with [[Erastes]]. Indirial has fought [[Kai]], [[Denner Weeks|Denner]], and [[Valin]], though he previously saved [[Kai]] and served as [[Kai]]'s first student.}}

== Abilities ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|As a [[Valinhall Travelers|Valinhall Traveler]] and [[Incarnation]], Indirial can summon weapons from the [[Valinhall armory]] and possesses the power to cut open a [[Valinhall Gate]]. He wields a chipped [[Dragon's Fang]] named [[Vasha]] and can make his [[sword]] vanish. His skills include wearing translucent green light or flickering [[ghost armor]], using [[liquid steel]] from [[Valinhall]], and utilizing a diamond to provide clarity and focus.}}

=== {{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Valinhall Traveler}} ===
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Zakareth]] seeks to recruit Indirial, an Overlord whose forearms are marked by shadowy [[chains]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c2">''City of Light'', chapter 2</ref><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c3">''City of Light'', chapter 3</ref><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c7">''City of Light'', chapter 7</ref> His left hand is encased in a spiked [[black gauntlet]] known as a [[Valinhall gatecrawler]], and he wields a long, cracked [[sword]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c4">''City of Light'', chapter 4</ref><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c7" /> Reminiscent of someone [[Valin]] knows, Indirial previously saved [[Simon]] and later requested his assistance.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c6">''City of Light'', chapter 6</ref> Hired by [[Leah's father]] to protect the ruling monarch, this son of Aleias is a [[Valinhall Travelers|Valinhall Traveler]] who possesses the ability to cut open a [[Valinhall Gate]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c7" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c11">''City of Light'', chapter 11</ref> During his time in [[Valinhall]], which lasted over an hour, he utilized an unorthodox application of a lesser-known power.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c9">''City of Light'', chapter 9</ref> After concluding a discussion with Feiora, he shouted warnings for people to retreat.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c10">''City of Light'', chapter 10</ref><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c11" /> The Overlord can manifest a plate of translucent green light as flickering [[ghost armor]] and possesses a grip comparable to an [[Ornheim golem]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c12">''City of Light'', chapter 12</ref><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c13">''City of Light'', chapter 13</ref> While attempting to cut a Gate, Indirial was found near death, sprawled upon the steps of a waystation.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c13" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c14">''City of Light'', chapter 14</ref>}}

=== {{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Prisoner of black ice}} ===
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Indirial was held suspended within a prison of black ice, where he utilized [[liquid steel]] from [[Valinhall]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c17">''City of Light'', chapter 17</ref> After being called [[stone]], he was warned by [[Zakareth]] that the survival of others depended upon his own.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c17" /> While acting as a voice of caution within [[Leah]]'s mind, he faced the reality that his wife and daughter had also been denied [[water]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c18">''City of Light'', chapter 18</ref><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c19">''City of Light'', chapter 19</ref> He was able to call upon [[steel]] to remain standing, even as he wielded a straight [[sword]] in his left hand and a [[Dragon's Fang]] in his right.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c19" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c20">''City of Light'', chapter 20</ref> Using a [[Valinhall]] diamond to filter his focus, he utilized his weapon [[Vasha]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c20" /> Though his presence hung over others like a banner, Indirial eventually succumbed to his [[chains]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c20" />}}

=== {{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Incarnation of Ragnarus}} ===
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|As a powerful avatar of [[the House]] wandering the outside world, Indirial serves as more than just an [[Incarnation]], acting as a trusted warrior and servant.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c20" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c21">''City of Light'', chapter 21</ref> Representing the [[Incarnation of Ragnarus]], this individual was last seen in the camp five days prior.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c21" /> Indirial was observed standing beside [[King Zakareth VI|King Zakareth]] wearing a cloak of shadows and arm [[chains]] that had been turned to [[steel]], leading [[Leah]] to suspect the King may have taken him.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c21" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c22">''City of Light'', chapter 22</ref> This [[Valinhall Incarnation]], whom [[Kai]] encountered on the tiles of the [[House of Blades]], felt both the [[destruction]] of [[Tartarus]] and [[Kai]]'s rage.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c22" /> As [[Kai]]'s first student, Indirial is an [[Incarnation]] who possesses [[Nye essence]], a [[Territory]], and the ability to summon weapons from the [[Valinhall armory]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c22" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c23">''City of Light'', chapter 23</ref>}}
<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">14</span></div>

=== {{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Sealed in the Territory}} ===
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Indirial is a Shadow{{!}}shadow-cloaked [[Incarnation]] with violet eyes who sits in the [[entry hall]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c24">''City of Light'', chapter 24</ref> Having been sealed into the [[Territory]], this corrupted being became an [[Incarnation]] after fighting another [[Valinhall Travelers|Valinhall Traveler]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c24" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c25">''City of Light'', chapter 25</ref> After attacking the [[House of Blades]], Indirial was sealed in [[the House]] and forced to embrace [[Valinhall]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c25" /><ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c26">''City of Light'', chapter 26</ref> While [[Leah]] has Indirial with her, [[Zakareth]] mentions his specific job.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c27">''City of Light'', chapter 27</ref> From within [[Valinhall]], Indirial oversees the day-to-day management of his realm.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c28">''City of Light'', chapter 28</ref>}}
<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">10</span></div>

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Indirial]] has violet eyes.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c24" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Indirial]] has been sealed into the [[Territory]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c24" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Indirial]] became an [[Incarnation]] after fighting another [[Valinhall Travelers|Valinhall Traveler]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c25" />}}</li>

== Notable quotes ==
* {{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|“And, if we tried anything, you know Indirial would kill us both.”<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c11" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Indirial, he…he fought me. He sealed me.” Valin’s face contorted with rage. “He stood with the Damascans.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c4" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Perhaps Indirial can even lure this Incarnation back into his home Territory."<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c8" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|“And the Valinhall Traveler, Indirial, son of Aleias.”<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c11" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|“I'm going to start cutting a Gate,” Indirial announced, his voice weak.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c14" />}}
